catalog_quote: Ударение обычно падает на последний слог корня (основы): удýн 'дрова', мисú 'маленький', кIушкIулá 'желтый', джыбы́н-дыр 'карманы', дáб-хер 'обманщик' и т. п. В то же время ударными являются аффиксы прилагательных -лы/-ли и -сыз: даьрт-лú 'грустный'. В глаголах всегда ударным является формант отрицания.

sources.citation: Alekseev, M. E. 2001. Khinalugskij jazyk. In Jazyki mira: Kavkazskie jazyki, pp. 460-469; stress section 2.1.2 on p. 462 — read from the full scanned volume PDF downloaded from the Institute of Linguistics RAN site (iling-ran.ru/staff_only/langworld_proto/static/pdf_volumes/), pages…
sources.quote: "Stress usually falls on the last syllable of the root (stem): udún 'firewood', misí 'small', k'ushk'ulá 'yellow', dzhybýn-dyr 'pockets', dáb-kher 'deceiver', etc. At the same time, the adjectival affixes -ly/-li and -syz are stressed: därt-lí 'sad'. In verbs, the negation formant is always stressed."

sources.quote: p. 93: 'The stress shifts to the added preverb (as the new first syllable), so that čä- is reduced to {/č/ + schwa}' ... 'Here, the stress is on čä- so that the non-aspirated affricate and the low vowel are maintained'; p. 109: 'since the stress of preverb constructions is on the first syllable, an is unstressed and reduced to {schwa + n}'; p. 88: 'Vowel length mostly depends on stress and emphasis'. No general stress section (article is on verb morphology), but it documents initial stress in polymorphemic (preverb) verbs from a modern DoBeS corpus, i.e. the verb-initial vs noun root-final spl
sources.note: Modern corpus-based (DoBeS) statement that preverb-verb constructions are initial-stressed (pp. 93, 109) — independent confirmation of the verb side of the morphology-conditioned system; downloaded and read now, should be added to the record as corroboration.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: 'The stress in a word in Xinaliq depends on the morphology of the word. Generally stress falls on the last vowel of the root of the word: gadá 'boy', q̇aqál 'back'. If a suffix beginning with a vowel is attached to a root ending in a vowel, it replaces the final vowel and takes the stress: ḳilí-u -> ḳilú ... In derivative words, if the derivation is created by a suffix attached to the root, the stress remains on the final vowel of the root: q̇aqál -> q̇aq̇álır, dáb -> dábxẹr. Listed below are exceptions ... mátıška, bášqap, tóq̄ud, hána, qárı, qíni, ḳä́vi, láǧın.'
